title: Momentum and its conservation; Impulse and force–time graphs
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics C: Mechanics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: D09-ap2#t2 term and clue written for the game; D09-ap2#t3 term and clue written for the game; D10-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; D10-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: D09-ap2#N.5, D10-1#N.4b, D09-ap2#N.10, D10-1#N.12.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Component
items.clue: The x or y part into which a vector is split.

items.label: Elastic collision
items.clue: The only kind of impact in which kinetic energy is conserved.

items.label: Crumple zone
items.clue: Car feature that lengthens the stopping time, making the average force smaller.

items.label: Impulse
items.clue: Vector in N s pointing along the resultant force, not necessarily along the motion.

questions.stem: An object of mass 4m at rest on a frictionless horizontal surface explodes into three pieces that slide along the surface. Immediately after the explosion, a piece of mass m moves at speed v in the +x-direction and a piece of mass 2m moves at speed 2v in the +y-direction. What is the speed of the third piece, of mass m?

Pucks A and B are at rest on level ice with negligible friction. Puck A has mass m, and puck B has mass 2m. Each puck is pushed by the same constant horizontal force F for the same time interval Δt. After the push, puck A has momentum of magnitude p_A. What is the magnitude of puck B's momentum after the push?

An open cart of mass 3m rolls at speed v₀ along a level track with negligible friction. A ball of mass m falls vertically into the cart and stays in it; just before it lands, the ball's speed is 4v₀. What is the speed of the cart, with the ball in it, just after the ball lands?

Two identical 0.50 kg gliders on an air track each move at 2.0 m s⁻¹ towards an obstacle. Glider 1 hits a steel buffer and bounces straight back at 2.0 m s⁻¹; the contact lasts 0.010 s. Glider 2 hits a foam pad and stops; the contact lasts 0.040 s. How many times larger is the average force on glider 1 than the average force on glider 2?

options.text: 1, as both gliders arrive with the same speed
